newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat -Spring bids mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat -Spring bids mostly higher.

text.p: Spring wheat cash bids were mostly higher on Tuesday amid slow farmer sales, dealers said.
"It's been dead," a Montana broker said. Farmers are engaged fieldwork, and April spring plantings in some areas appeared to be on schedule.
Residents along three rivers in the southeastern corner of South Dakota may face uncertainty for two weeks or more, as a massive, melting snowpack in the north is expected to unleash floods.
State officials have no firm estimate on how many homes and businesses might be at risk along the Big Sioux, Vermillion and James Rivers, all of which drain into the Missouri River.
Forecasters said cool weather would bring a longer, lower flood, while a quick warm-up would spark a faster, higher one.

Temperatures will go as high as the 60s (Fahrenheit) later this week but cooler weather the past few days appears to have slowed the melting process to the north, where snow was still almost knee-deep, and eased the threat of a sudden flood.

The record snowfall along the North and South Dakota border and in Minnesota was causing problems in two other drainage areas besides the upper Missouri basin. They include the headwaters region of the Minnesota River, which flows eventually into the Mississippi, and the Red River, which runs northward out of North Dakota to Winnipeg and Hudson Bay.
